notes:
Summary: Enterprise CCaaS provider evaluating Redwood for real-time agent assist. Primary goal is streaming suggestions to agents during live calls/chat with a strict latency SLO and deterministic fallbacks.

Key quotes and ask: "Need first suggestion under 120ms p95; streaming tokens must start returning within 50-80ms for agent UX." - Head of Product. Also: "If our primary model degrades during spikes we need automatic fallback to smaller model with graceful context trimming." - SVP Ops.

Technical requirements (from PoC scoping):
- Workload: 1000 concurrent agent sessions during normal hours; target 10k concurrent during peak campaigns/holiday spikes.
- Latency/Throughput targets: p95 time-to-first-token <= 120ms; median <= 60ms; sustained throughput 2M tokens/day.
- Streaming: support token-level streaming to UI with rollback if hallucination thresholds crossed.
- Guardrails: real-time content filters, intent confidence scoring, and sync to enterprise DLP rules.
- Tool-calling: integration with ServiceNow and internal CRM via webhook/tool APIs (must call out ticket-create, update, fetch-customer-context).
- Model preference: open-model baseline (Llama-like family acceptable) with option to host fine-tuned conversation model; quantization/FP16 options desired for Dedicated.
- Reliability: automatic fallback (regional + model variant) and routing based on latency/cost policy; 99.5% availability SLA desired for critical routes.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-session latency traces, and per-route eval dashboards.

Security/compliance notes: SOC2 in place but they require Redwood artifacts; data residency: primary US, EU for EU customers; KMS integration and audit logging mandatory.

POC scope: 2-week multi-load test: steady-state 1k agents + spike test to 10k, validate first-token latency, streaming behavior, tool-calling APIs, and fallback quality. Deliverables: perf report, quality metrics vs baseline, recommended batching/quantization config from Redwood Optimize.

Stakeholders: Head of Product (Maya Lin), SVP Ops (Carlos Vega), Head of Security (Renee Morales).

Sales notes: pricing sensitivity but willing to commit to dedicated capacity if latency and reliability pass PoC. Close target Q2 2026.

Recent pain: previous vendor suffered 800ms+ tail latency during campaign spikes; they want deterministic behavior and easier runbooks for on-call teams.

Next steps (short): share PoC network diagram (Jordan), finalize NDA addendum for logging retention (legal), schedule PO approval meeting (Finance)
